gate_policy: A candidate must land within atol + rtol * |reference| of the fp32 reference on EVERY element of EVERY case. This is the acceptance criterion the workload bundle's own benchmark applies to this operator family, read from here so the task and the acceptance run cannot drift into two definitions of correct. It replaces a gate derived at run time from the production implementation's own distance to the reference. That gate bounded a mean relative error and an SNR, and neither can see what this one exists to catch: a kernel that truncates its split-k or K-warp partial sums to bf16 before reducing them measures about 0.0017 mean relative error and about 51 dB, comfortably inside any aggregate bound worth setting, while missing this tolerance on 6-11 percent of the output. Aggregates average that tail away. The tolerance is not tight for a kernel that accumulates in fp32: measured at n=k=6144, fp32 partial sums match the reference on every element at split counts 2, 4, 8 and 16, at about 113 dB. So the gate admits any reduction order and rejects a truncated accumulator, which is the distinction it exists to make. The production implementation's own accuracy is measured and reported beside every case for context; it does not move the bar, and it does not clear it at every shape.
